text: Writing a separate test for every boundary value is tedious and you'll still miss cases. Fuzz testing flips that: give the test a parameter, and Forge calls it hundreds of times with random input.
Any typed parameter on a test function gets fuzzed automatically — Forge runs it 256 times by default, reporting a failure the moment any run breaks your assertion.
Most functions don't accept any uint256 — there are real constraints. vm.assume throws away runs outside your range; bound clamps the value into range instead, so every run counts.
The fuzz table in foundry.toml tunes the campaign — raise runs from the 256 default for a wider search, and set a fixed seed to make a failing run reproducible.
A fuzz test still only calls one function, once, per run. It doesn't test sequences across functions and actors — that's exactly what invariant testing adds, next.
